patients.summary: Retired postal worker with long-standing poorly controlled type 2 diabetes who joins in 2018, develops B12 deficiency on a vegan diet and metformin (2021), CKD 3b and iron deficiency (2022), a neurogenic bladder from diabetic autonomic neuropathy (2024), and a pyloric adenocarcinoma treated by distal gastrectomy (2026), with overflow retention in July 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
62 yo M transferring care. Retired from the postal service a couple of years ago. Says he went to his old office "whenever something came up," which wasn't often, and he is hoping for closer follow-up here.

Diabetes since about 1996, on metformin and nightly glargine for years. Doesn't check sugars much, maybe twice a week, fasting numbers 160s-220s by his report. No lows he knows of. Numb feet for several years, worse at night, no wounds. Told he had diabetic changes in the back of the eyes, last eye exam a few years ago. BP and cholesterol treated for a long time.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, glargine 30 units qhs, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. No known drug allergies.
PMH as above. No surgeries.
FH: father had type 2 diabetes. Mother had stomach cancer (gastric adenocarcinoma). Maternal grandfather had colon cancer.
SH: grew up in northern Europe, came here as a young man. Married, lives with wife in Hatfield. Vegan for many years, for ethical reasons. Never smoked, does not drink.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT unremarkable, no thyromegaly. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext: no edema. Feet: skin intact, no calluses or ulcers, DP pulses palpable bilaterally. Monofilament reduced at the toes and forefoot bilaterally, vibration reduced at both great toes.

A/P:
1. Type 2 DM, poorly controlled by history, with neuropathy and retinopathy. A1c, CMP, urine albumin today. Talked about tightening things up; he would like to see the numbers first. Continue metformin and glargine 30.
2. HTN, near goal today. Continue lisinopril.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
4. Retinopathy: referral to ophthalmology for a dilated exam.
5. Health maintenance: hep C and HIV screening today. Tdap and flu today. Has never had colon cancer screening; not interested in colonoscopy right now, will do a FIT kit. Records request to prior office.

Follow up 3 months.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Philip, your labs are back. Your A1c is 9.4, which is well above where we want it (under 8 for you, ideally lower). Kidney function, potassium and liver tests look fine. Blood count is normal. LDL cholesterol is in a good range on the atorvastatin. Urine protein test was normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative.

I'd like to talk about the sugar numbers at your next visit in January. In the meantime, if you can check fasting sugars 3-4 mornings a week and bring the log, that would help a lot.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office, 14 pages, covering 2011-2018. Scanned to chart.

Summary for PCP review: visits roughly once a year, several gaps of more than a year. Problem list there: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetic neuropathy, diabetic retinopathy. Meds match what patient reported (metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 u qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40). Last A1c in their records 9.8 (2017). Eye clinic letter from 2015 mentions retinopathy both eyes. No colonoscopy or FIT on file. No allergies listed.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Letter to patient. Repeat yearly unless he decides on colonoscopy.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

We saw Mr. Hall on 11/29/2018 for a dilated diabetic eye examination.

Visual acuity with correction 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS. Pupils normal. IOP 15 and 16. Anterior segment: clear lenses for age.
Dilated fundus exam: diabetic retinopathy in both eyes. No macular edema on exam or OCT. Optic nerves healthy.

Impression: diabetic retinopathy OU without macular edema.
Plan: return in 12 months, sooner for any change in vision. Better glucose control will help protect his eyes, and we have encouraged this.

Thank you for the opportunity to participate in his care.

Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Brought a log, about 10 fasting readings since Christmas, 148-231. Taking everything as prescribed, he says. No lows. Feet the same, numb, no sores. Eye exam done in November, letter reviewed.

O: see vitals. Feet: skin intact, no ulcers. Point-of-care A1c drawn.

A/P: DM2, A1c 9.1, a hair better than October but still high. Offered to move glargine up 2 units every few days to a fasting target of 100-150, or to add a once-weekly injection. He would rather not change insulin right now; worried about having a low while driving and says he is going to "cut back on bread and pasta." Respected, revisit in spring. Continue current regimen.
HTN at goal-ish. Continue lisinopril.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Refill request: metformin
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy fax requesting 90-day supply of metformin 1000 mg BID; previous prescriber was the old office. Last A1c 9.1 on 1/24. Sent 90-day supply with 3 refills under PCP per refill protocol.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: Diabetes, Hypertension
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt here for f/u. Feels fine. Has been walking more now that the weather turned, about 30 min most days. Diet changes "some." Fasting sugars 140s-190s. No hypoglycemia.

Exam: NAD. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet unchanged, skin intact.

A1c 8.9.

A/P
- DM2: slow drift down. Again offered glargine titration; he'd like to keep going with diet and walking until fall. OK. Continue metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 u.
- HTN: BP acceptable. Continue lisinopril 20. BMP today.
- HLD: atorvastatin 40.
All chronic meds now prescribed from here, 90-day supplies sent.
RTC after summer / annual physical in October.

documents.title: insulin pens cost
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, the pharmacy says my insulin pens will cost more starting next month because of the plan. Is there a different one that is cheaper? I don't want to stop it. Philip

documents.title: RE: insulin pens cost
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Mr. Hall, I checked with your plan's formulary. The glargine pen you use is still the preferred one; the price change is from the deductible resetting, not the drug. The pharmacy can run it as a 90-day supply which lowers the per-month cost a bit. I sent a new 90-day prescription. Please don't skip doses. Call us if the cost is still a problem and we can look at assistance programs.

procedures.procedure: Preventive visit, established patient, 40-64

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 63M.

Interval: no hospital visits or new problems. Walked a lot this summer, "backed off" with the colder weather. Sugars mostly 150-200 fasting. Takes meds daily, occasionally forgets the evening metformin. Eye exam due in December, scheduled.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 u qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
SH: married, retired postal carrier. Vegan. Never smoker, no alcohol.
FH unchanged (father DM2, mother gastric cancer, maternal GF colon cancer).
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: Gen well. HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx normal. Neck: no thyromegaly or adenopathy. CV: RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT, no masses. GU deferred. Ext: no edema. Skin: no concerning lesions. Neuro: diminished vibration at both great toes, monofilament reduced at toes; strength normal; gait normal. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance: flu shot today. FIT kit again; colonoscopy discussed, still prefers FIT. Tdap current (2018).
2. DM2 with neuropathy, retinopathy: labs today. Will discuss results by portal.
3. HTN: continue.
4. HLD: continue statin.
RTC 3-4 mo.

documents.title: Lab results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Philip, A1c came back 9.3, so we are back up from the spring. Kidney function is about where it was last year, and cholesterol is in range. Blood count is normal. Urine protein normal.

I'd really like to revisit insulin adjustment when you come in this winter. Please return the FIT kit in the next couple of weeks.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative x2 years. Result letter sent.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Re: Philip Hall, DOB 07/22/1956. Seen 12/05/2019.

BCVA 20/25 OU. IOP 16/15. Dilated exam: diabetic retinopathy both eyes, unchanged from last year. No macular edema; OCT macula normal thickness OU.

Assessment: diabetic retinopathy OU, stable, no macular edema.
Plan: annual exam. Patient counseled on glycemic and blood pressure control.

Allergies: none known.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for DM check. Says the holidays were "the usual." Fasting sugars 150-210 on the few days he checked. No hypoglycemia. No foot sores. Numbness unchanged. Eye exam in December stable per letter.

Vitals reviewed. Feet: skin intact, no calluses, monofilament reduced at toes as before.

A1c 9.0.

Plan: We talked again about adding something or titrating glargine. He is still reluctant; his main worry is lows. Gave him the titration plan in writing in case he changes his mind (raise 2 units every 3 days if fasting over 150, stop if under 100). Continue metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30, lisinopril, atorvastatin.
Return in April.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home with wife helping with the tablet. Identity verified with DOB. April visit cancelled when the office limited in-person care.

Doing OK. Staying home, wife does the shopping. Walking around the yard and down to the end of the road most days. Fasting sugars by his meter 140s-180s the last couple weeks. No lows. No new foot problems; he looks at his feet in the shower.

Meds unchanged, has 90-day supplies at home.

A/P: DM2, HTN, HLD stable by report. Labs deferred until the fall physical unless something comes up. He knows to call for any foot wound. Physical in October.

procedures.procedure: Preventive visit, established patient, 40-64

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64 y/o man, annual visit. Masked, first in-person visit since February.

Interval: has mostly stayed home this year. Less walking since summer. Eating more bread and rice than he'd like, admits. Fasting sugars higher, often around 200. No lows. No chest pain or breathlessness. Feet numb as before. Missed the FIT kit this year, says it is in a drawer.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
PHQ-2: 1 (a little down with the isolation, not most days).

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin unremarkable. Feet: intact skin, pulses present, monofilament decreased at toes bilaterally, vibration decreased at great toes. Gait normal.

A/P:
1. Prevention: flu vaccine today. FIT: he'll find the kit and send it in.
2. DM2 with complications: labs today. Discussed again that if the A1c is still over 9 I would strongly recommend we raise the glargine.
3. HTN, HLD: continue.
4. Mood: situational, he and his wife are keeping each other company; will recheck at next visit.
RTC Jan/Feb.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Philip, your A1c is 9.6, the highest since you joined us. Kidney function is a little lower than last year (creatinine 1.31) but OK for now; we'll keep watching it. Cholesterol is fine. Urine protein normal.

I'd recommend raising your glargine using the plan I gave you in February: go up 2 units every 3 days while your morning sugar is over 150, and stop raising if any morning is under 100. Let me know what you think.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you doctor. I would like to try getting back to walking and less bread first. I will see you after new year and if it is not better we can do the insulin.

documents.title: Refill: glargine pens
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request for glargine pens, 30 units qhs, 90-day supply, plus pen needles. Last visit 10/5, A1c 9.6. Refilled per protocol. FIT still not returned; reminder letter mailed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: Fatigue and Gait Change
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, feet worse, walking is harder.

HPI: 64M with long-standing DM2 (since ~1996) with neuropathy and retinopathy. Wife made this appointment. Over the past several months he has been more and more tired, napping in the afternoons, which is new. The numbness in his feet has crept up and now he feels unsteady, "like walking on a mattress," worse in the dark. Pins and needles in his hands too, and in the legs above the usual area. Wife says he has been forgetting things: missed a dentist appointment, repeated the same story twice in a day. He thinks she is exaggerating but admits he lost track of what day it was last week. No falls yet. No chest pain, no black stools, no bleeding he's noticed. No alcohol. Diet: strict vegan for years, does not take a B12 supplement. On metformin since the late 1990s.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.

Exam: pale, conjunctival pallor. Alert, conversant, but gave the date as the 8th (it is the 11th); knew month, year and place. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Neuro: strength 5/5 throughout. Vibration sense decreased in both legs to the ankles; joint position sense impaired at both great toes. Reflexes diminished at the ankles. Sways with eyes closed. Gait wide-based and cautious. Sensation reduced to light touch in a stocking distribution.

A/P:
1. Fatigue, pallor, new posterior column signs, memory lapses in a vegan on long-term metformin: B12 deficiency at the top of the list, with diabetic neuropathy contributing to the foot findings. CBC with smear, B12, folate, homocysteine, TSH, CMP drawn here today. Will call with results.
2. Gait: fall precautions reviewed; no driving at night until we sort this out.
3. DM2: A1c not repeated today, due next visit. Continue current meds for now.

Called lab at 5 pm: CBC back, Hgb 9.2, MCV 112, smear with hypersegmented neutrophils. Called patient, B12 pending, expect it tomorrow.

medications.sig: Inject 1 mL (1000 mcg) into the muscle daily for 7 days, then weekly for 4 weeks, then monthly

orders.order: Nurse visit: B12 injection and home injection teaching

documents.title: Results call: B12 deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spoke with patient and wife on speaker. B12 118 (low), homocysteine 41 (high), folate normal, TSH normal. Together with yesterday's macrocytic anemia and smear, this is vitamin B12 deficiency with neurologic involvement. Likely cause is the long vegan diet without supplement plus decades of metformin.

Plan: cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM daily x 7 days, then weekly x 4, then monthly, long term. Nurse visit tomorrow for the first shot and to teach wife to give the rest at home; Rx for vials, syringes and needles sent. Explained the nerve symptoms may take months to improve and some may not fully recover. Recheck CBC in ~6 weeks. They agree.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: B12 Injection
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt here with wife. Cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg (1 mL) IM given L deltoid, tolerated well. Taught wife IM technique on the deltoid and thigh with return demonstration x2 using a practice pad; she will give tomorrow's dose and was confident. Reviewed schedule on a printed calendar: daily through 1/19, then weekly x4 (Wednesdays), then monthly starting late February. Sharps container provided. Wife has the vials from the pharmacy. Call with any questions.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: B12 Deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks into B12 replacement. Wife has given every dose on schedule, one more weekly shot left then monthly. He says the tiredness is "half of what it was," no more afternoon naps most days. Hands tingle less. Feet still numb, walking a bit steadier but he uses the railing on stairs. Wife thinks his memory is better.

Exam: color better. Oriented x3, date correct. Vibration still reduced in the legs to the ankles, position sense still off at the toes. Gait still a little wide, steadier than January.

CBC: Hgb 11.0 (from 9.2), MCV 101 (from 112). Moving the right way.

A/P: B12 deficiency anemia, responding. Continue monthly IM after the last weekly dose. CBC, B12 and A1c in April. COVID vaccine: eligible soon with his conditions, encouraged to sign up at the pharmacy.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: B12 Deficiency, Diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Monthly B12 shots now, wife gives them the first Monday of the month. Energy close to normal, he's back to his walks. Memory: no new episodes his wife has noticed. Hands no longer tingle. Feet numb as they were before all this, maybe a little worse at the toes. Unsteadiness much better, no falls. Both COVID shots done at the pharmacy.

O: oriented, conversational, tells a coherent history. Vibration reduced at the toes only now. Position sense intact at the ankles, slightly off at the great toes. Gait normal base, steady turn.

Labs drawn today, results by portal.

A/P
1. B12 deficiency anemia: clinically much improved. Continue cyanocobalamin monthly indefinitely (diet + metformin).
2. DM2: A1c drawn. He'd still like to try lifestyle first.
3. HTN: continue lisinopril.
4. BMP today.
RTC August for Welcome to Medicare visit.

documents.title: April labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Philip, good news on the blood count: hemoglobin is 12.4, nearly normal, and the red cells are back to normal size. B12 level is 690, right where it should be on the shots. A1c is 9.0, unchanged. Creatinine 1.42, a bit higher than last fall, we'll recheck in August. Keep up the monthly injections.

documents.title: B12 needles
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. My wife says we are almost out of the small needles for the B12. We have vials left. Can you send the needles and syringes to the pharmacy? Thanks, Philip Hall

documents.title: RE: B12 needles
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Mr. Hall, the syringes and needles were sent to your pharmacy this morning with refills for the year. They should be ready this afternoon.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Dear Colleague,

Philip Hall (DOB 07/22/1956) returned 06/17/2021 for a diabetic eye exam; his 2020 exam was postponed during the pandemic.

VA cc 20/25 OD, 20/30 OS. IOP 15/16. Lenses clear. Dilated fundus: diabetic retinopathy OU, similar to 2019 photos. No macular edema on OCT.

Assessment: diabetic retinopathy OU without macular edema, stable.
Plan: annual follow-up.

Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Welcome to Medicare Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial preventive physical exam. Turned 65 last month.

Health risk review: lives with wife in a one-level house. Independent in daily activities, still drives in daylight. No falls this year. Hearing OK. Vision: eye exam June, stable. Exercise: walks 30-40 min most mornings. Diet vegan; taking B12 shots monthly now. No tobacco or alcohol. Seat belt always. Home has smoke detectors.
PHQ-9: 2.
Cognition: oriented, recalls 3/3 words, clock drawing normal.
Advance directive: his wife is his health care agent; form given to complete at home.

Interval: energy good. Feet numb, no wounds. No urinary or bowel complaints.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM monthly. NKDA.

Exam: well. HEENT normal, neck no masses. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Skin: no lesions of concern. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament reduced at toes, vibration reduced at great toes. Gait steady.

Plan:
- Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine albumin.
- Vaccines: flu in the fall (high-dose now that he is 65). Pneumococcal and shingles vaccines to discuss at the fall visit. COVID booster when offered.
- Colon screening: FIT overdue, new kit given; he is open to colonoscopy "next year."
- Written screening schedule given.

documents.title: Results from your Medicare visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Philip, a few things from your labs:
- Hemoglobin 12.6, holding steady.
- Creatinine 1.55. This is higher again (1.31 last October, 1.42 in April). Diabetes and blood pressure over many years are the usual reasons. I'd like to recheck in about 3 months, and if it keeps rising we'll get a kidney specialist involved.
- A1c 9.2.
- Cholesterol fine, urine protein normal.
Please avoid ibuprofen/naproxen-type pain relievers; acetaminophen is fine.

procedures.procedure: Immunization administration

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza vaccine 0.7 mL IM R deltoid. Screening questions answered no. VIS given. Observed 15 min, no reaction. FIT kit from August still not returned; reminded.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes / Kidney Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Feels well. Booster at the pharmacy last month, sore arm only. B12 monthly at home. Walking less now that it's dark early. Sugars ~170-230 fasting. No lows. No NSAIDs. No urinary symptoms, no swelling.

O: vitals reviewed. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet intact.

Labs today (called in this afternoon): creatinine 1.74, continuing to rise (1.18 at joining, 1.55 in August). A1c 9.5.

A/P:
1. Rising creatinine with long-standing diabetes and hypertension: referring to nephrology for evaluation. Continue lisinopril. Avoid NSAIDs.
2. DM2: A1c 9.5. Recommended again raising glargine; he says he'll "think about it after the holidays." Documented.
3. B12 deficiency: stable on monthly IM.
RTC after nephrology visit.

documents.title: Kidney specialist appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hello Mr. Hall, your nephrology (kidney) appointment is scheduled for Friday January 21 at 10:20 am at the outside nephrology group's office. They will mail you a new patient packet. Please bring your medication list. Call us if you need to change it.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
NEPHROLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 01/21/2022
Patient: Philip Hall, DOB 07/22/1956
Referred by: primary care, for rising serum creatinine

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for asking us to evaluate Mr. Hall, a 65-year-old retired postal worker with long-standing type 2 diabetes complicated by neuropathy and retinopathy, hypertension and hyperlipidemia, treated a year ago for vitamin B12 deficiency.

He tells us that for about two months he has felt increasingly worn out and gets short of breath walking uphill or carrying groceries. He has had no chest pain, no racing heartbeat and no fainting. No urinary complaints, no leg swelling. No NSAID use.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, insulin glargine 30 units at bedtime, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Allergies: none known.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Vegan diet.

Exam: BP 140/85, pulse 88, respirations 18. Comfortable at rest. Heart: regular rhythm, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear on both sides. No peripheral edema.

Labs drawn today: hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, creatinine 1.9 mg/dL, BUN 36 mg/dL, potassium 5.5 mEq/L. Prior urine albumin/creatinine ratios from your office have not been elevated.

Impression:
1. Chronic kidney disease stage G3b, most consistent with diabetic and hypertensive kidney disease, non-albuminuric pattern. Creatinine has risen steadily over three years.
2. Mild hyperkalemia, 5.5, on an ACE inhibitor with a high-potassium plant-based diet.
3. Anemia, now microcytic (it was macrocytic during his B12 deficiency last year). Iron deficiency is the leading concern and could explain his fatigue and exertional breathlessness. Would appreciate your evaluation with iron studies.

Recommendations:
- Continue lisinopril 20 mg for now.
- Met with our renal dietitian today: lower-potassium choices within a vegan diet (portion limits on potatoes, tomatoes, bananas, beans; leaching technique for root vegetables).
- Repeat BMP in 1-2 weeks; can be drawn at your office.
- Avoid NSAIDs and IV contrast without prophylaxis.
- Return to nephrology in 12 months with labs, sooner for potassium over 5.8 or creatinine over 2.3.

We appreciate the referral.

Nephrology

documents.title: Office Visit: Fatigue, Anemia, CKD
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his nephrology consult last week; letter reviewed.

HPI: Two to three months of fatigue and getting winded on hills and stairs. Not as bad as last winter, he says, but clearly there. No chest pressure, no palpitations, no orthopnea, no ankle swelling. No black or bloody stools, no other bleeding. Appetite fine. Still strict vegan; B12 shots monthly at home on schedule. Last CBC here in August was 12.6 with MCV 86; at nephrology hemoglobin 9.8 with MCV 72.

Exam: pale conjunctivae. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Abdomen soft, nontender. Neuro unchanged.

ECG today: normal sinus rhythm, no ischemic changes.

A/P:
1. Microcytic anemia, new since August, after B12 replacement. Suspect iron deficiency (iron-poor diet, plus a big jump in red cell production once the B12 was replaced). Iron studies today. He has never had a colonoscopy, FITs negative 2018 and 2019. Will refer to GI if iron is low.
2. Exertional dyspnea and fatigue: ECG normal, lungs clear, no signs of heart failure; most likely the anemia. Will recheck symptoms once treated.
3. CKD 3b (new from nephrology): potassium recheck today per their plan, dietitian advice reviewed. Continue lisinopril.
4. DM2: A1c due in spring.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with vitamin C-rich food, not with tea

orders.reason: Iron deficiency anemia; no prior colonoscopy

documents.title: Results: Iron Deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt. Ferritin 7, transferrin saturation 5%: iron deficiency. Potassium down to 5.0 on the diet changes; creatinine 1.86, stable.

Plan: ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, take with orange juice or fruit, away from tea/coffee; may darken stools and constipate. Diet alone unlikely to correct this. Because he is 65 and has never had a colonoscopy, referring to GI for colonoscopy as part of the workup. He agreed this time. CBC in about 3 months.

procedures.procedure: Colonoscopy, diagnostic

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ENDOSCOPY CENTER: COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Procedure date: 03/22/2022
Patient: Philip Hall, 65 M
Indication: iron deficiency anemia; no prior colonoscopy; maternal grandfather with colon cancer.
Allergies: NKDA.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care with propofol. ASA class III.
Prep: split-dose PEG, excellent throughout.

Findings: digital rectal exam normal. The scope was advanced to the cecum, confirmed by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve; terminal ileum intubated and normal. Withdrawal time 11 minutes. No polyps, masses, angioectasias or colitis. Normal retroflexion in the rectum. No blood seen.

Impression: normal colonoscopy to the terminal ileum. No colonic source of iron deficiency.

Recommendations:
- Continue oral iron per PCP. If iron deficiency does not correct on oral iron, upper endoscopy would be the next step.
- Repeat colonoscopy for screening in 10 years.
- Resume prior diet and medications.

Gastroenterology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: Iron Deficiency, Diabetes

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit date: 01/19/2024
Patient: Philip Hall, 67-year-old man
Referring: primary care
Reason: difficulty voiding, night-time leakage

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for sending Mr. Hall. He has had type 2 diabetes for close to three decades, poorly controlled, with peripheral neuropathy and retinopathy, as well as stage 3b CKD and a history of B12 deficiency on replacement.

History: over roughly the past year he has found it steadily harder to start his stream. The flow is weak and intermittent, and he dribbles after he believes he has finished. At times he feels the need to go but cannot get the bladder to empty. For the last several weeks he has woken at night with damp underwear, unaware of having leaked. He denies dysuria, suprapubic pain, fevers and blood in the urine. He admits he has missed a number of medical appointments over the past year.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, insulin glargine 30 units nightly, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol; retired from the postal service.
Family: father with type 2 diabetes; mother with gastric adenocarcinoma; maternal grandfather with colon cancer.

Exam: the bladder can be felt above the pubic bone and is mildly tender to percussion. External genitalia normal. DRE: prostate about 25 g, smooth, no nodules. Focused neurologic exam: reduced sensation in both lower extremities, ankle jerks diminished on both sides.

Bladder scan after an attempted void: post-void residual 360 mL. UA and PSA from your office normal.

Impression: incomplete bladder emptying with overflow leakage from a neurogenic, poorly contracting bladder. With no history of spinal or pelvic injury, the most likely cause is diabetic autonomic neuropathy affecting the sacral nerve supply to the bladder. The prostate is not enlarged.

Plan:
- Drained in clinic by straight catheter.
- Clean intermittent self-catheterization four times daily, taught today by our nurse with good return demonstration. Hydrophilic 14 Fr catheters; supply order sent (may need a prior authorization from your office).
- Timed voiding before each catheterization. Avoid anticholinergic medications.
- Return in about 4 months with catheterization volume diary.

Urology

events.reason: Upper abdominal pain, early satiety, poor intake, weight loss

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT of the abdomen and pelvis with IV and oral contrast, IV contrast given with IV hydration for reduced kidney function. The stomach is distended with retained fluid and food debris, and oral contrast has passed only slowly into the duodenum, suggesting delayed gastric emptying. There is focal narrowing of the distal stomach with circumferential wall thickening of the distal antrum and pylorus. No enlarged perigastric or regional lymph nodes. Liver without focal lesion. No ascites or peritoneal nodularity. Pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands unremarkable. Kidneys symmetric without hydronephrosis. Urinary bladder unremarkable. No bone lesions.
reports.conclusion: Distended stomach with retained contents suggesting delayed gastric emptying, with focal narrowing and wall thickening of the distal stomach at the pylorus. Endoscopy recommended. No lymphadenopathy or liver lesion.

reports.text: Specimen: stomach, pyloric channel, endoscopic biopsies (6 fragments). Microscopic: gastric mucosa infiltrated by malignant glands. Immunohistochemistry: HER2 1+ (negative). Mismatch repair proteins MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6 retained (proficient). No Helicobacter organisms identified on immunostain.
reports.conclusion: Stomach, pylorus, biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma. HER2 negative (IHC 1+). Mismatch repair proficient.

reports.text: CT of the chest with IV contrast for staging, given with IV hydration. Abdomen and pelvis imaged 01/09/2026. Lungs clear without nodules or consolidation. No pleural or pericardial effusion. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. Heart normal in size.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease.

documents.title: Discharge Summary: General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL: GENERAL SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 01/09/2026    Discharged: 01/14/2026
Patient: Philip Hall, 69 M    Allergies: NKDA

Principal diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the stomach, pyloric region, with partial gastric outlet narrowing.
Secondary: mild iron-deficiency anemia; type 2 diabetes, long-standing and poorly controlled, with peripheral neuropathy and retinopathy; CKD stage 3b; neurogenic bladder; prior vitamin B12 deficiency on replacement; hypertension; hyperlipidemia.

History: referred from the ED. Several months of a dull, constant ache below the sternum that worsens with eating, so he has been eating less. Early fullness and intermittent nausea; he has not vomited recently, but over the few days before admission he could take only a few spoonfuls at a time. Roughly 15 lb unintentional weight loss over the last few months (76.0 kg on admission). Mother had gastric adenocarcinoma.

Exam on admission: mild epigastric tenderness without a palpable mass. Cardiopulmonary exam unremarkable. Neurologic: no focal deficit.

Workup:
- Labs: hemoglobin 11.2, MCV 78, ferritin 11, consistent with mild iron deficiency. Liver enzymes and bilirubin normal. Creatinine 1.79 (baseline per PCP records).
- CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast 1/9 (with IV hydration): distended stomach with retained contents suggesting delayed emptying, focal narrowing and wall thickening of the distal stomach at the pylorus; no lymphadenopathy, no liver lesions, no ascites.
- EGD 1/10: narrowed pyloric channel with abnormal mucosa, biopsied.
- Pathology 1/12: invasive adenocarcinoma; HER2 negative (1+); MMR proficient; no H. pylori.
- CT chest with contrast 1/12: no thoracic disease. Creatinine unchanged after contrast.

Hospital course: NPO with IV fluids and NG decompression for 24 hours, then clear and full liquids, then soft diet in small portions, tolerated without nausea by day 4. Insulin adjusted while intake was low; home glargine dose resumed once eating. Diagnosis discussed with patient and wife. Case presented at multidisciplinary tumor board planning; outpatient EUS arranged.

Discharge medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, insulin glargine 30 units nightly, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM monthly, NEW ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Diet: soft, small frequent meals; vegan protein supplement shakes.
Follow-up: EUS 1/27; surgical oncology 2/3; PCP within 1 week.

General Surgery

documents.title: Surgical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
SURGICAL ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit: 02/03/2026
Re: Philip Hall, 69-year-old man

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Mr. Hall with a newly diagnosed adenocarcinoma of the gastric pylorus causing partial outlet obstruction. Biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma, HER2 negative, MMR proficient. CT abdomen/pelvis and chest: no nodal or distant disease. EUS: uT2 N0.

He is tolerating a soft diet in small portions. Weight has been stable since discharge. Comorbidities include long-standing type 2 diabetes with peripheral and autonomic neuropathy and retinopathy, CKD 3b (creatinine around 1.8), neurogenic bladder, hypertension and hyperlipidemia. NKDA. No prior abdominal surgery.

Exam: thin, no distress. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no palpable mass, no hernias.

Tumor board discussion (02/02/2026): localized cT2 N0 M0 distal gastric cancer with outlet narrowing. Perioperative chemotherapy was considered; given the obstruction, his pre-existing neuropathy and his kidney function, the board recommended upfront surgery, with adjuvant therapy decided on final pathology.

Plan:
- Staging laparoscopy with peritoneal washings, then laparoscopic distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy and Roux-en-Y reconstruction if no peritoneal disease. Scheduled 02/17/2026.
- Risks, benefits and alternatives discussed with patient and wife; consent signed.
- Preoperative medical evaluation with you, please.
- Nutrition: continue protein supplements; dietitian visit before surgery.

Surgical Oncology

reports.text: Specimen: distal stomach with attached omentum (distal gastrectomy), and separately submitted lymph node stations. Gross: ulcerated lesion at the pylorus. Microscopic: invasive adenocarcinoma invading the muscularis propria, not through it. No lymphovascular or perineural invasion identified. Proximal and distal margins negative. Lymph nodes: 0 of 27 involved. Peritoneal washings: negative for malignant cells.
reports.conclusion: Distal gastrectomy: invasive adenocarcinoma of the pylorus, pT2 N0 (0/27), margins negative. Peritoneal washings negative. AJCC pathologic stage IB.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date: 02/17/2026
Preoperative diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the gastric pylorus, cT2 N0 M0, with outlet narrowing.
Postoperative diagnosis: same; no peritoneal disease.
Procedures: diagnostic laparoscopy with peritoneal washings; laparoscopic distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy; Roux-en-Y gastrojejunostomy.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
Findings: no ascites, peritoneal implants or liver lesions. Tumor confined to the pyloric region, no serosal involvement visible. No enlarged nodes.
Estimated blood loss: 150 mL. Fluids: crystalloid. Urine: Foley placed after induction, clear urine.
Specimens: distal stomach and omentum; lymph node stations; washings.
Complications: none. Patient extubated and taken to PACU in stable condition.

Surgical Oncology

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission: 02/17/2026  Discharge: 02/23/2026
Patient: Philip Hall, 69 M. NKDA.
Procedure: staging laparoscopy (washings negative), laparoscopic distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy and Roux-en-Y reconstruction, 02/17.

Course: uncomplicated. Diet advanced from clear liquids on POD 2 to soft small meals by POD 4. Pain controlled with acetaminophen and short-term low-dose oxycodone, off opioids by POD 4. Foley removed POD 2; given his neurogenic bladder, bladder scans were followed and he resumed intermittent self-catheterization in hospital before discharge, residuals acceptable after re-teaching. Glucose managed with basal-bolus insulin, home glargine resumed POD 3; metformin resumed at discharge with creatinine stable at baseline. Lisinopril resumed POD 3. Hemoglobin stable. Ambulating independently.

Final pathology (02/20): invasive adenocarcinoma of the pylorus, pT2 N0 (0/27 nodes), margins negative, washings negative. Stage IB.

Discharge medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, insulin glargine 30 units nightly, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM monthly; acetaminophen as needed.
Diet: post-gastrectomy diet, 6 small meals, separate liquids from solids.
Follow-up: surgical oncology 2 weeks; medical oncology 3/10; PCP within 1 week.

MEDICAL ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit date: 03/10/2026
Re: Philip Hall, 69 M, retired postal worker

Dear Doctor,

We met Mr. Hall and his wife to discuss treatment after resection of a gastric adenocarcinoma of the pylorus. He underwent laparoscopic distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy and Roux-en-Y reconstruction on 02/17/2026 following negative staging laparoscopy. Pathology: pT2 N0 (0/27 nodes), R0, no lymphovascular or perineural invasion; HER2 negative, MMR proficient. AJCC stage IB.

He is recovering well, eating six small meals a day. ECOG 1. Comorbid diabetes with neuropathy, CKD 3b, neurogenic bladder on intermittent catheterization. NKDA.

Exam: thin, well-healing incisions, abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly, no supraclavicular nodes.

Assessment and recommendation: after upfront D2 resection with an adequate node count and no high-risk features, adjuvant chemotherapy or chemoradiation is not expected to add meaningful benefit for pT2 N0 disease, and his pre-existing neuropathy and kidney function would add risk. We recommend surveillance.

Surveillance plan: visits every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months to year 5. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast (with IV hydration) every 6 months for 2 years; first scan in August. Lifelong B12 replacement (already on monthly injections) and periodic iron studies after gastrectomy.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Regional hospital ED. Seen 07/12/2026.
Patient: Philip Hall, 69 M. Allergies: NKDA.

Chief complaint: constant leaking of urine, can't empty bladder.

HPI: 69-year-old man with neurogenic bladder first evaluated by urology in 2024, long-standing poorly controlled type 2 diabetes with peripheral neuropathy, and gastric adenocarcinoma diagnosed this year (distal gastrectomy in February). For about four months he has had constant dribbling of urine, including after he voids, and a persistent sense that the bladder is not empty. He is changing his underwear several times a day and the symptoms have slowly worsened. Despite going to the bathroom frequently he never feels relieved. No burning, no blood in the urine, no suprapubic pain. His wife adds that he often struggles to get started and there can be a long wait before a good stream comes. When asked, he acknowledges past episodes of retention for which he used intermittent catheterization; he stopped some time ago.

Meds (per patient list): metformin 1000 mg BID, insulin glargine 30 units at bedtime, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, retired postal worker.
Family: father with type 2 diabetes; mother with gastric adenocarcinoma; maternal grandfather with colon cancer.

Exam: well-appearing, afebrile. Abdomen soft, nontender; a mass is palpable in the lower abdomen consistent with a distended bladder. Healed laparoscopic incisions. DRE: smooth prostate of normal size, no nodules. Neuro: decreased sensation in the feet and legs consistent with his diabetic neuropathy; strength intact.

Results: HbA1c 9.2%. BMP: creatinine 1.76, at his known baseline; no acute kidney injury; electrolytes unremarkable. Urinalysis negative for infection and blood.
Bedside bladder ultrasound after voiding: post-void residual 450 mL, significant retention.

ED course: 16 Fr Foley catheter placed with return of clear urine; patient comfortable afterward.

Impression: chronic urinary retention with overflow incontinence from known neurogenic bladder; not infected; renal function at baseline.
Disposition: discharged home with Foley and leg bag, catheter care teaching done. Urology follow-up within 1 week for voiding trial. PCP follow-up in 1-2 days. Return for fever, catheter blockage, blood in urine or abdominal pain.

UROLOGY
Visit: 07/21/2026
Re: Philip Hall, DOB 07/22/1956

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Hall was seen after his 07/12 ED visit for retention with overflow (PVR 450 mL), his first urology visit since 05/2024. He had stopped clean intermittent catheterization in 2025, restarted it after his February gastrectomy, then stopped again in March.

Voiding trial: Foley removed this morning, bladder backfilled. He voided small amounts with straining. Post-void residual by bladder scan 410 mL.

Assessment: neurogenic bladder from diabetic autonomic neuropathy with chronic retention; failed voiding trial.
Plan: clean intermittent catheterization five times daily, re-taught today with good technique; catheter supplies reordered (new prior authorization will be requested). Avoid anticholinergics. Return in 6 weeks with a catheter volume diary, sooner for fever or hematuria.

NKDA.

MEDICAL ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit 08/18/2026
Re: Philip Hall, 70 M

Six months after distal gastrectomy for stage IB (pT2 N0) adenocarcinoma of the pylorus. He feels well, eating small frequent meals, weight steady since spring. No abdominal pain, vomiting or dysphagia. Back on intermittent catheterization after an ED visit for urinary retention in July.

Exam: no supraclavicular nodes, abdomen soft and nontender, incisions well healed.

CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 08/14/2026: postsurgical change, no recurrence or metastasis.

Plan: continue surveillance. Next visit and CT in February 2027. Continue B12 and iron; we will check iron studies with his next labs.
